transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Um… I’m here because I’ve been having these nagging thoughts at work. I’m a designer, and I keep worrying I’ve missed some tiny mistake in a layout, or that I sent a client the wrong version of something. I can usually see that it’s probably fine, but my mind just keeps circling back to it. It’s not, like, dramatic or anything… but it’s been bothering me enough that I thought I should ask about it.
Do you find yourself doing anything specific, like checking or redoing work, to try to ease those worries or make sure everything is perfect?

Yeah… I mean, I do check, but I try to keep it reasonable. Before I submit something, I’ll usually re-open the file, compare the layers, re-save it, and kind of mentally walk through the design choices one more time. Sometimes more than once, if I’m being honest.

It doesn’t take over my whole day or anything, but it definitely slows me down. And I think it makes me feel a little less… free creatively, if that makes sense. Like I’m not just trusting the work as much as I used to.

Do you ever have thoughts that feel intrusive or unwanted, which cause you significant distress, and do you feel the need to do something specific—like checking, counting, or repeating actions—to neutralize those thoughts or prevent something bad from happening?

Yes… I think so. I don’t want to overstate it, because it’s not like I’m panicking all day, but I do get these thoughts that feel kind of unwanted and hard to shake—like, “What if I missed some tiny mistake in the layout?” or “What if I sent the client the wrong version?”

Even when I can look at it and think, “No, it’s probably fine,” my mind keeps circling back to it. So I guess that counts as intrusive? I’m not sure if I’m describing it right.

Do these thoughts or the need to check your work ever cause you significant distress or interfere with other parts of your life, like your personal relationships, sleep, or overall enjoyment of your job?

A little, yes… I mean, I’m still getting my work done, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. But I have started missing some internal deadlines because I keep holding things back to check them again.

And… I guess it’s affecting how I approach the work, too. I’ll sometimes avoid bolder design ideas because I’m worried I’ll overlook something or make a mistake that reflects badly on me. I’ve been hoping to move more toward a creative director role eventually, and I worry this could hurt my chances if I can’t trust myself more. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have these thoughts and the need to check your work been happening most days, and have they been going on for at least two weeks?

I’m not totally sure, honestly. It feels like it’s been happening pretty often, but I haven’t really tracked it day by day. I don’t want to give you the wrong answer.

I’d say there have been stretches where it’s most days, especially when I’m busy with client work, but I’m not sure if I can confidently say it’s been every day or exactly two weeks. Is “most days” more about how it feels overall, or literally counting the days?
Looking back, would you say these thoughts and the need to check your work have been happening on most days, even if not every single day?

Yes… looking back, I think I would say most days. Maybe not every single day, and some days it’s quieter, but it does keep coming up a lot.

It’s that nagging thought that I’ve missed some tiny mistake in a layout, or that I sent the wrong version to a client. Even when I can tell myself, “This is probably fine,” my mind sort of circles back to it anyway. So… yes, I think “most days” is fair to say.
Do these checking behaviors ever take up a lot of time—like more than an hour a day—or cause you a lot of stress, even if you’re still able to get your work done?

I don’t think it takes over my whole day, no… not usually. I’d be hesitant to say it’s more than an hour every day, because I’m still getting things done.

But before I submit work now, I’ll re-open the file, compare the layers, re-save it, and then sometimes sort of mentally walk through every design choice one more time. It’s not dramatic, exactly, but it does slow me down. And it makes me feel less… free, creatively, if that makes sense. Like I’m more focused on making sure nothing is wrong than just doing the work confidently.
Are these thoughts about making mistakes or sending the wrong version something you experience as intrusive and unwanted, rather than just normal concerns about doing your job well?

Yes… I think that’s right. I don’t want to make it sound more serious than it is, because of course I do care about doing good work and not making mistakes.

But it feels a little different from normal double-checking. The thought kind of pops back in even after I’ve already looked at the file and can see it’s probably fine. Like, “What if there’s one tiny thing I missed?” or “What if I sent the wrong version?” And I don’t really want to be thinking about it again, but my mind keeps circling back to it. Does that make sense?

When these intrusive thoughts come up, do you feel driven to perform your checking behaviors in a specific way or according to certain rules, like needing to check things a certain number of times or in a particular order?

Not really a number, no. I don’t think I have to check it exactly three times or anything like that.

It’s more like… I feel like I need to go through a little sequence before I can send it. I’ll re-open the file, look through the layers, compare that it’s the right version, re-save it, and then sometimes I mentally walk through the design choices one more time. It’s not a formal rule, I guess, but if I don’t do it, I feel unsettled.

I know that probably sounds like normal carefulness, and maybe it partly is, but it does slow me down and makes me less relaxed creatively.

Have you noticed any other kinds of unwanted thoughts, images, or urges that pop into your mind that feel intrusive and bothersome, or do you ever feel the need to do anything else repeatedly to try to manage anxiety or uncertainty?

Not really other kinds, I don’t think… or at least nothing that stands out the same way.

It’s mostly what I mentioned — these nagging thoughts that I’ve missed some tiny mistake in a layout, or that I somehow sent the wrong version to a client. And even when I can look at it and see, logically, it’s probably fine, my mind kind of keeps coming back to it anyway. Like it doesn’t fully let it go.

I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing you mean, but that’s the main one that’s been bothering me.
Have you noticed any other types of unwanted or intrusive thoughts, images, or urges that come into your mind and feel disturbing or hard to control, even if they’re not related to your work?

I don’t think so… not in a big way, anyway. I mean, I don’t have other disturbing images or urges that I can think of.

It’s really mostly the work-related thoughts — like that I’ve missed some tiny mistake in a layout, or that I sent the wrong version to a client. Even when I can see it’s probably fine, it just keeps coming back into my head and I have a hard time letting it go.

I’m not sure if that answers what you’re asking.

Have you noticed any other situations outside of work where you feel the need to check things repeatedly or have intrusive thoughts that are hard to control, even if they don’t seem related to your job?

I don’t think so, no… at least nothing that I’ve really noticed.

I mean, I’m sure I double-check normal things sometimes, like anyone would, but it doesn’t feel like the same kind of stuck feeling I get with work files. Outside of work, I can’t really think of a situation where it keeps coming back or where I feel I have to keep checking.

I hope that makes sense — I’m not trying to leave anything out, I just don’t think there’s much there.

Have you ever experienced any other types of intrusive, unwanted thoughts, images, or urges that significantly upset you or are hard to control, even if they don’t relate to your work or checking behaviors?

I don’t think there are other types, really… or at least nothing that feels significant like that.

The thing I came in about is mostly these nagging thoughts with my design work — like I’ve missed some tiny mistake in a layout, or maybe I sent the wrong version to a client. And even when I can look at it and tell myself it’s probably fine, my mind just kind of circles back to it anyway.

I know that may sound small, but it gets stuck in my head. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do these thoughts bother you even when you’re not actively checking your work—like when you’re away from your computer or trying to relax—and do they make you feel anxious or upset?

Yes… I think so. I mean, not all the time, and I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but sometimes even when I’m away from my computer, I’ll still get this nagging thought like, what if I missed some tiny mistake in that layout, or what if I sent the wrong version to the client?

Even if I can tell myself it’s probably fine, my mind kind of circles back to it. It’s annoying, and it does make me anxious… maybe more than I’d like to admit. Does that make sense?
Can you estimate how much time these checking behaviors and intrusive thoughts take up in a typical day—like, do they add up to more than an hour in total, or is it usually less than that?

It’s usually less than an hour, I think… at least most days. I don’t want to exaggerate it.

Before I submit work now, I’ll re-open the file, compare the layers, re-save it, and sometimes sort of mentally walk through every design choice one more time. It doesn’t take over my whole day or anything, but it does slow me down. And I guess it makes me feel less free creatively, if that makes sense.

Maybe some days it adds up more than I realize, but I’d say generally it’s under an hour.

It doesn’t take over my whole day or anything, but it does slow me down. And I guess it makes me feel less free creatively, if that makes sense.

Maybe some days it adds up more than I realize, but I’d say generally it’s under an hour.
